cues.text: Cloud centralises scalable resources; edge computing puts processing close to the data source.
Fog often describes intermediary distributed nodes between devices and the cloud.
Multi-access edge computing, or MEC, brings compute and storage near access networks for mobility and latency-sensitive services.
Look at the diagram in the notes.
A sensor or programmable logic controller sends information to a local gateway.
The gateway passes it to an edge compute node.
From there we have two important paths: the edge can trigger a local action, and filtered events can be sent onward to cloud analytics.
This explains why not every raw sensor reading needs to travel across the WAN.
Edge can reduce WAN delay and bandwidth, allow local decisions during backhaul failure, and reduce exposure by minimising transmitted data.
It does not automatically remove the cloud, costs or security risks.
Edge hardware has resource limits and is distributed physically, so it needs updates, monitoring, secure identity, local storage and consistency management.
The cloud remains valuable for global analytics, model training, coordination and archival.
Choose placement based on the delay budget, data volume, connectivity, compute resources, privacy and failover requirements.
